title: Scaling low-latency inference with Gimlet Cloud and Cerebras (Gimlet Labs, Sep 28 2026)
quote: Together, Gimlet and Cerebras plan to deploy 100 megawatts of Cerebras-powered inference capacity. The first Cerebras-powered Gimlet Cloud datacenter is expected to come online later this year, delivering speeds of up to 3,000 tokens per second for demanding agentic and real-time applications. Gimlet uses disaggregation techniques including Prefill-Decode, Attention-FFN, and Speculative Decoding disaggregation to run these phases across different types of silicon. The Cerebras architecture is particularly well suited to memory-intensive inference operations, including the token-generation phase of large language models, where latency and responsiveness are critical.

title: The emerging role of SRAM-centric chips in AI inference (Gimlet Labs, Mar 5 2026)
quote: The H100 has 50 MB in SRAM, rising to 126 MB for the B200, whereas SRAM-centric architectures invest more heavily: B200 (dual-die) ~1600 mm² 4 nm 126 MB L2; Groq LPU v1 725 mm² 14 nm 230 MB; Cerebras WSE-3 46255 mm² 5 nm 44 GB. Off-chip memory bandwidth scales O(1/sqrt(N)) with chip area, whereas on-chip memory bandwidth scales closer to O(1) with chip area but is fundamentally capped by total chip size and zero-sum with compute capacity. Even Cerebras, the largest SRAM-centric chip which uses an entire wafer, "only" has 44 GB of SRAM storage, so weights for large models need to be distributed across multiple chips. As the CTO of d-Matrix noted, "Industry benchmarks show that compute performance has grown roughly 3x every two years, while memory bandwidth has lagged at just 1.6x."

quote: FP4 Tensor Core: 144 PFLOPS | 72 PFLOPS (Specification in Sparse | Dense). FP8/FP6 Tensor Core: 72 PFLOPS. FP16/BF16 Tensor Core: 36 PFLOPS. TF32 Tensor Core: 18 PFLOPS. Total Memory: 1.4 TB. NVLink GPU-to-GPU Bandwidth: 1.8 TB/s.

title: Cerebras announces third generation Wafer-Scale Engine (press release, Mar 2024)
quote: 4 trillion transistors; 900,000 AI optimized compute cores; 125 petaflops of peak AI performance; 44GB on-chip SRAM; 5nm TSMC process.

title: Introducing Cerebras Inference: AI at Instant Speed (Cerebras, Aug 27 2024)
quote: With our unique wafer-scale design, we are able to integrate 44GB of SRAM on a single chip. In total, the WSE-3 has 21 petabytes/s of aggregate memory bandwidth – 7,000x that of an H100. A H100 has 3.3 TB/s of memory bandwidth.
